There is no Chrome on this machine and the download was blocked, so `hyperframes snapshot` failed. ## What I added - **Overlay element**: a `#screen-fx` div as the last child of `#main`, sitting above the title and caption (`z-index: 100`) from 0s to 10s. - **Look**: dark horizontal scanlines every 4px, a faint red/green/blue vertical stripe pattern, and darkened corners and edges with a slight glow in the centre. - **Root sizing**: `#main` now has an explicit 1920×1080 box with `overflow: hidden`, so the overlay has a full frame to fill. The effect is static CSS, with no flicker or rolling band, because the project has no GSAP timeline to drive motion. ## Things to know - **Hand-built, not from the registry**: the project's registry at `localhost:4890` lists `filmed-screen` and `scan-band`, but returns 404 for everything except `data-chart`. I did not pull from the public registry, since the project points elsewhere. - **No gap report sent**: the search came back empty because the items couldn't be fetched, not because the catalog lacks the effect, so I skipped the `hyperframes feedback` report. - **Lint still fails**: `hyperframes lint` reports a missing `window.__timelines` registration, exactly as it did before my change. I left that alone. - **Stray folders**: running the CLI created `.hyperframes/` and `.cache/` inside `/workspace`, because the home directory here is the workspace. They are CLI state and safe to delete. To check the look once a browser is available, set `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` and run `npx hyperframes snapshot --at 1,5,9`. answer:
The screen effect is wired into `index.html` and covers the full frame for all 10 seconds, but I couldn't render a frame to check it visually: this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg. What I could check: `hyperframes timeline` still shows both clips at their original times, and lint reports the same two findings as before my change.

I used the registry's `yt-screen-warp` component ("On-Screen Display Effect"), installed to `compositions/components/yt-screen-warp.html`. In `index.html`:

- **Overlay:** a scanline, pixel-grid, vignette and sheen layer sits on top of everything as the last element in the frame.
- **Tilt:** the title card and caption are now inside a `#screen` wrapper with the component's slight 3D perspective, so the picture looks like a monitor seen slightly off-axis.
- **Root sizing:** `#main` is now explicitly 1920×1080 with overflow hidden, so the overlay has a frame to fill.

Two places where I departed from the component's defaults:

- **Always on:** the component ships with fade-in/fade-out helpers that need a GSAP timeline. Since you want the effect over the whole composition, I set the overlay permanently visible in CSS instead, so it's there from frame 0 with no script.
- **Overscan:** tilting a full-frame wrapper pulls its left edge up to about 50px inside the frame, which would leave a strip without scanlines. I extended the overlay 64px past each edge to close that; the cost is a somewhat weaker vignette at the borders.

If you'd rather have a flat, head-on screen, remove `class="yt-screen-warp3d"` from `#screen` and the `#screen-fx` inset override.

Two things you should know about the project itself:

- **Lint error that predates this change:** `main` has no `window.__timelines` registration, which lint flags as an error and which adds a 45-second wait to every render. Adding `data-no-timeline` to the `#main` element is the fix lint suggests; I left it alone since it's outside what you asked.
- **Registry is mostly empty:** `hyperframes.json` points at `https://localhost:4890/registry`, which returned 404 for 451 of the 455 items in its manifest. The catalog search came back with nothing for that reason, so I found the component by reading the manifest directly.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      *,
      *::before,
      *::after {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }
      body {
        background: transparent;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      /* ---- yt-screen-warp ---------------------------------------------------
         Make footage read as a physical display: add .yt-screen-warp3d to the
         media WRAPPER (subtle perspective), and place .yt-screen-fx overlay
         inside it (pixel grid + scanlines + vignette + sheen). */
      .yt-screen-warp3d {
        transform: perspective(1400px) rotateY(-3.5deg) rotateX(1.6deg);
      }
      .yt-screen-fx {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
        opacity: 0;
        background:
          /* sheen */
          linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09) 0%, transparent 30%),
          /* scanlines */
          repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          /* pixel grid */

<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Launch teaser</title>
<style>body{margin:0;background:#111;color:#fafafa;font-family:sans-serif}
#main{position:relative;width:1920px;height:1080px;overflow:hidden}
#screen{position:absolute;inset:0}
/* ---- yt-screen-warp (from compositions/components/yt-screen-warp.html) ----
   Make footage read as a physical display: .yt-screen-warp3d on the media
   wrapper (subtle perspective), .yt-screen-fx overlay as its last child
   (pixel grid + scanlines + vignette + sheen). */
.yt-screen-warp3d{transform:perspective(1400px) rotateY(-3.5deg) rotateX(1.6deg)}
.yt-screen-fx{position:absolute;inset:0;pointer-events:none;opacity:0;
background:
linear-gradient(115deg,rgba(255,255,255,.09) 0%,transparent 30%),
repeating-linear-gradient(0deg,rgba(0,0,0,.1) 0 1px,transparent 1px 3px),
repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(0,0,0,.06) 0 1px,transparent 1px 4px);
box-shadow:inset 0 0 90px rgba(0,0,0,.4),inset 0 0 8px rgba(0,0,0,.5)}
/* On for the full runtime, so no ytScreenOn/ytScreenOff cues. The tilt pulls
   the wrapper's left edge up to ~50px inside the frame; overscan the overlay
   so the scanlines still reach every edge. */
#screen-fx{inset:-64px;opacity:1}
</style>

The composition now has a full-frame screen overlay (scanlines, pixel grid, vignette and sheen) on from the first frame for the whole 10 seconds. I couldn't render it here (no Chrome or FFmpeg on this machine), so it is checked by `hyperframes lint` only (0 errors, 0 warnings), not by eye.

- **Component:** I installed the registry's "On-Screen Display Effect" (`yt-screen-warp`) with `hyperframes add`, which wrote `compositions/components/yt-screen-warp.html` and `hyperframes.lock.json`; the CLI also left a `.hyperframes/` cache/config folder in the project.
- **Wiring in `index.html`:** the overlay is a new `#screen-fx` clip (0–10s, track 3) as the last child of `#main`, layered above the title and caption. `#main` is now a fixed 1920×1080 positioned box so the overlay covers exactly the frame.
- **Timeline:** the project had no GSAP timeline, so I added GSAP 3.14.2 and registered one for `main`. It holds the overlay on from time 0 rather than using the component's half-second fade-in helper. This also clears the "missing timeline registration" lint error the project had before.

I left out the component's 3D tilt (`.yt-screen-warp3d`). It is meant for a media wrapper inside the frame, and tilting the root composition would skew the whole video. If you want it, the footage needs an inner wrapper to tilt — say so and I'll add it.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      *,
      *::before,
      *::after {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }
      body {
        background: transparent;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      /* ---- yt-screen-warp ---------------------------------------------------
         Make footage read as a physical display: add .yt-screen-warp3d to the
         media WRAPPER (subtle perspective), and place .yt-screen-fx overlay
         inside it (pixel grid + scanlines + vignette + sheen). */
      .yt-screen-warp3d {
        transform: perspective(1400px) rotateY(-3.5deg) rotateX(1.6deg);
      }
      .yt-screen-fx {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
        opacity: 0;
        background:
          /* sheen */
          linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09) 0%, transparent 30%),
          /* scanlines */
          repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          /* pixel grid */
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px);
        box-shadow:
          inset 0 0 90px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4),
          inset 0 0 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
      }
      /* self-preview stand-in */
      #yt-sw-wrap {
        position: absolute;
        left: 360px;
        top: 190px;
        width: 1200px;
        height: 700px;
        border-radius: 18px;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      #yt-sw-fill {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        /* Placeholder footage: L3 of the ink over the dark ground, plus a 3px
           achromatic hatch so the plate reads as a media surface, not an empty box. */
        background:
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18);
        box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14);
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        font-family: "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
        font-weight: 700;
        font-size: 92px;
        color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.93);
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Self-preview wrapper. WIRING: copy the two CSS classes; add
         class="yt-screen-warp3d" to your media wrapper and
         <div class="yt-screen-fx" id="yt-my-fx"></div> as its LAST child. Then:

           ytScreenOn(tl, "#yt-my-fx", 2.0);
           ytScreenOff(tl, "#yt-my-fx", 8.0);
    -->
    <div
      id="yt-sw-root"
      data-composition-id="yt-screen-warp"
      data-start="0"
      data-duration="4"
      data-width="1920"
      data-height="1080"
    >
      <div id="yt-sw-wrap" class="yt-screen-warp3d">
        <div id="yt-sw-fill">on screen</div>
        <div class="yt-screen-fx" id="yt-sw-fx"></div>
      </div>
      <div
        id="yt-sw-drv"
        class="clip"
        data-start="0"
        data-duration="4"
        data-track-index="0"
        style="position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; opacity: 0; pointer-events: none"
      ></div>
    </div>
    <script>
      (function () {
        window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};

        // ---- copy these helpers into the host script ----
        window.ytScreenOn = function (tl, target, at) {
          tl.to(target, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, at);
        };
        window.ytScreenOff = function (tl, target, at) {
          tl.to(target, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: "power2.in" }, at);
        };

        // Self-preview timeline.
        var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
        gsap.set("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 0, scale: 0.96 });
        tl.to("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, 0.2);
        window.ytScreenOn(tl, "#yt-sw-fx", 0.8);
        window.ytScreenOff(tl, "#yt-sw-fx", 3.1);
        tl.to("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 0, duration: 0.35, ease: "power2.in" }, 3.5);
        tl.set("#yt-sw-root", { visibility: "hidden" }, 3.98);
        window.__timelines["yt-screen-warp"] = tl;
      })();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>

answer:
The scanline overlay is now on the whole composition, but I couldn't render a frame to look at it: this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg, and the Chrome download failed. `hyperframes lint` passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

I installed the registry's "On-Screen Display Effect" component (`yt-screen-warp`) with `hyperframes add` and wired its overlay into `index.html`:

- **Overlay:** a `.yt-screen-fx` div is the last child of `#main`, so the scanlines, pixel grid, edge vignette and sheen sit above both clips across the full 1920×1080 frame.
- **Timing:** it is on at full strength from the first frame to the last, rather than using the component's half-second fade-in helper.
- **Root sizing:** `#main` now has an explicit 1920×1080 box so the overlay fills the frame instead of only the text's height.
- **`data-no-timeline`:** I added this to the root. The file already failed lint for having no registered timeline, and the overlay is static, so this is the documented opt-out. Remove it if you add GSAP animation later.

Decision for you: the component also ships a subtle 3D tilt class (`yt-screen-warp3d`) meant for an inset media wrapper. I left it off because tilting the full frame would pull one edge in by about 40px and crop the opposite one. Adding the class to `#main` turns it on if you want the off-axis look — say so and I'll add it.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      *,
      *::before,
      *::after {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }
      body {
        background: transparent;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      /* ---- yt-screen-warp ---------------------------------------------------
         Make footage read as a physical display: add .yt-screen-warp3d to the
         media WRAPPER (subtle perspective), and place .yt-screen-fx overlay
         inside it (pixel grid + scanlines + vignette + sheen). */
      .yt-screen-warp3d {
        transform: perspective(1400px) rotateY(-3.5deg) rotateX(1.6deg);
      }
      .yt-screen-fx {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
        opacity: 0;
        background:
          /* sheen */
          linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09) 0%, transparent 30%),
          /* scanlines */
          repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          /* pixel grid */
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px);
        box-shadow:
          inset 0 0 90px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4),
          inset 0 0 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
      }
      /* self-preview stand-in */
      #yt-sw-wrap {
        position: absolute;
        left: 360px;
        top: 190px;
        width: 1200px;
        height: 700px;
        border-radius: 18px;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      #yt-sw-fill {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        /* Placeholder footage: L3 of the ink over the dark ground, plus a 3px
           achromatic hatch so the plate reads as a media surface, not an empty box. */
        background:
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18);
        box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14);
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        font-family: "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
        font-weight: 700;
        font-size: 92px;
        color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.93);
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Self-preview wrapper. WIRING: copy the two CSS classes; add
         class="yt-screen-warp3d" to your media wrapper and
         <div class="yt-screen-fx" id="yt-my-fx"></div> as its LAST child. Then:

           ytScreenOn(tl, "#yt-my-fx", 2.0);
           ytScreenOff(tl, "#yt-my-fx", 8.0);
    -->
    <div
      id="yt-sw-root"
      data-composition-id="yt-screen-warp"
      data-start="0"
      data-duration="4"
      data-width="1920"
      data-height="1080"
    >
      <div id="yt-sw-wrap" class="yt-screen-warp3d">
        <div id="yt-sw-fill">on screen</div>
        <div class="yt-screen-fx" id="yt-sw-fx"></div>
      </div>
      <div
        id="yt-sw-drv"
        class="clip"
        data-start="0"
        data-duration="4"
        data-track-index="0"
        style="position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; opacity: 0; pointer-events: none"
      ></div>
    </div>
    <script>
      (function () {
        window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};

        // ---- copy these helpers into the host script ----
        window.ytScreenOn = function (tl, target, at) {
          tl.to(target, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, at);
        };
        window.ytScreenOff = function (tl, target, at) {
          tl.to(target, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: "power2.in" }, at);
        };

        // Self-preview timeline.
        var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
        gsap.set("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 0, scale: 0.96 });
        tl.to("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, 0.2);
        window.ytScreenOn(tl, "#yt-sw-fx", 0.8);
        window.ytScreenOff(tl, "#yt-sw-fx", 3.1);
        tl.to("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 0, duration: 0.35, ease: "power2.in" }, 3.5);
        tl.set("#yt-sw-root", { visibility: "hidden" }, 3.98);
        window.__timelines["yt-screen-warp"] = tl;
      })();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>

answer:
The scanline screen overlay is now on the whole composition for the full 10 seconds, but I couldn't render a frame to look at it: this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg. `hyperframes lint` reports nothing new from the change.

- **Source of the effect:** I installed the `yt-screen-warp` component ("On-Screen Display Effect") from your project registry with `hyperframes add`. It layers scanlines, a pixel grid, a vignette and a sheen.
- **Wiring in `index.html`:** the overlay is a new `#screen-fx` clip, the last child of `#main`, running 0–10s on its own track above the title and caption. I gave `#main` an explicit 1920×1080 positioned box so the overlay covers exactly the frame.
- **Always on:** the component ships the overlay hidden and fades it in from a GSAP timeline. I set it permanently visible in CSS instead, so it is there from the first frame and the composition still needs no script.
- **Tilt left out:** the component also has a slight 3D perspective tilt meant for an inset media panel. On a full-frame composition it would pull the edges inside the frame and leave strips without scanlines, so I didn't apply it.

The install also added `compositions/components/yt-screen-warp.html`, a `registryItems` entry in `hyperframes.json`, `hyperframes.lock.json` and a `.hyperframes/` folder.

Lint still shows the one error and one warning it showed before I touched anything: the composition registers no timeline. Adding `data-no-timeline` to `#main` clears both (checked in a scratch copy) and skips a 45-second wait on every render. I left it alone since it's outside what you asked — say if you want it added.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      *,
      *::before,
      *::after {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }
      body {
        background: transparent;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      /* ---- yt-screen-warp ---------------------------------------------------
         Make footage read as a physical display: add .yt-screen-warp3d to the
         media WRAPPER (subtle perspective), and place .yt-screen-fx overlay
         inside it (pixel grid + scanlines + vignette + sheen). */
      .yt-screen-warp3d {
        transform: perspective(1400px) rotateY(-3.5deg) rotateX(1.6deg);
      }
      .yt-screen-fx {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
        opacity: 0;
        background:
          /* sheen */
          linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09) 0%, transparent 30%),
          /* scanlines */
          repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          /* pixel grid */
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px);
        box-shadow:
          inset 0 0 90px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4),
          inset 0 0 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
      }
      /* self-preview stand-in */
      #yt-sw-wrap {
        position: absolute;
        left: 360px;
        top: 190px;
        width: 1200px;
        height: 700px;
        border-radius: 18px;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      #yt-sw-fill {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        /* Placeholder footage: L3 of the ink over the dark ground, plus a 3px
           achromatic hatch so the plate reads as a media surface, not an empty box. */
        background:
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18);
        box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14);
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        font-family: "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
        font-weight: 700;
        font-size: 92px;
        color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.93);
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Self-preview wrapper. WIRING: copy the two CSS classes; add
         class="yt-screen-warp3d" to your media wrapper and
         <div class="yt-screen-fx" id="yt-my-fx"></div> as its LAST child. Then:

           ytScreenOn(tl, "#yt-my-fx", 2.0);
           ytScreenOff(tl, "#yt-my-fx", 8.0);
    -->
    <div
      id="yt-sw-root"
      data-composition-id="yt-screen-warp"
      data-start="0"
      data-duration="4"
      data-width="1920"
      data-height="1080"
    >
      <div id="yt-sw-wrap" class="yt-screen-warp3d">
        <div id="yt-sw-fill">on screen</div>
        <div class="yt-screen-fx" id="yt-sw-fx"></div>
      </div>
      <div
        id="yt-sw-drv"
        class="clip"
        data-start="0"
        data-duration="4"
        data-track-index="0"
        style="position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; opacity: 0; pointer-events: none"
      ></div>
    </div>
    <script>
      (function () {
        window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};

        // ---- copy these helpers into the host script ----
        window.ytScreenOn = function (tl, target, at) {
          tl.to(target, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, at);
        };
        window.ytScreenOff = function (tl, target, at) {
          tl.to(target, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: "power2.in" }, at);
        };

        // Self-preview timeline.
        var tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
        gsap.set("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 0, scale: 0.96 });
        tl.to("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, 0.2);
        window.ytScreenOn(tl, "#yt-sw-fx", 0.8);
        window.ytScreenOff(tl, "#yt-sw-fx", 3.1);
        tl.to("#yt-sw-wrap", { opacity: 0, duration: 0.35, ease: "power2.in" }, 3.5);
        tl.set("#yt-sw-root", { visibility: "hidden" }, 3.98);
        window.__timelines["yt-screen-warp"] = tl;
      })();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>

/* On-screen display effect, from compositions/components/yt-screen-warp.html:
   sheen + scanlines + pixel grid + vignette so the footage reads as a physical
   display. The component ships it at opacity 0 for timeline fades; here it is
   on for the whole composition. */

  z-index:10;
  pointer-events:none;

    inset 0 0 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
}

answer:
The teaser now has the registry's "On-Screen Display Effect" (`yt-screen-warp`) wired over the whole frame. `hyperframes lint` passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings, but I couldn't render or snapshot it because this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg, so the look is unverified visually.

What changed:

- **Installed the component** with `hyperframes add yt-screen-warp`, which wrote `compositions/components/yt-screen-warp.html` and recorded it in `hyperframes.json` and `hyperframes.lock.json`.
- **Wired it into `index.html`**:
  - The overlay (scanlines, pixel grid, vignette, sheen) is a full-frame layer above both clips.
  - It switches on at 0s through the component's `ytScreenOn` helper and stays on to the end of the 10s.
  - The component's 3D-warp class is on the `#main` root.
  - GSAP is loaded and a `main` timeline registered; the file had neither before, and lint was failing on the missing timeline.

Two things you may want different:

- **Fade-in:** the helper fades the effect in over the first 0.5s, so the very first frames show it only partially. If you want it at full strength from frame 0, that is a one-line change.
- **Tilt:** the warp tilts the entire frame slightly, so by my arithmetic about 40px at the left edge shows bare background and about the same is cropped on the right. The title and caption sit at top-left and stay in frame. Removing `class="yt-screen-warp3d"` from `#main` gives a flat screen with the scanlines still on.

The CLI also created a `.hyperframes/` folder in the workspace (its own config and cache, since the home directory here is the workspace); it is not part of the composition.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      *,
      *::before,
      *::after {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }
      body {
        background: transparent;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      /* ---- yt-screen-warp ---------------------------------------------------
         Make footage read as a physical display: add .yt-screen-warp3d to the
         media WRAPPER (subtle perspective), and place .yt-screen-fx overlay
         inside it (pixel grid + scanlines + vignette + sheen). */
      .yt-screen-warp3d {
        transform: perspective(1400px) rotateY(-3.5deg) rotateX(1.6deg);
      }
      .yt-screen-fx {
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
        opacity: 0;
        background:
          /* sheen */
          linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09) 0%, transparent 30%),
          /* scanlines */
          repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
          /* pixel grid */
          repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px);
        box-shadow:
          inset 0 0 90px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4),

<!--
  Grain Overlay — animated film grain texture.

  Usage: paste this snippet into your composition's HTML.
  The overlay covers the full viewport with pointer-events: none
  so it sits on top of all content without blocking interaction.

  Customize:
  - opacity: adjust .grain-texture opacity (default 0.15)
  - speed: change animation duration (default 0.5s)
  - texture: swap the background URL for a different pattern
  - z-index: adjust #grain-overlay z-index to layer correctly
-->

<div
  id="grain-overlay"
  style="
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    pointer-events: none;
    z-index: 100;
  "
>
  <div class="grain-texture"></div>
</div>

<style>
  @keyframes hf-grain-noise {
    0%,
    100% {
      transform: translate(0, 0);
    }
    10% {
      transform: translate(-5%, -5%);
    }
    20% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    30% {
      transform: translate(5%, -10%);
    }
    40% {
      transform: translate(-5%, 15%);
    }
    50% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    60% {
      transform: translate(15%, 0);
    }
    70% {
      transform: translate(0, 10%);
    }
    80% {
      transform: translate(-15%, 0);
    }
    90% {
      transform: translate(10%, 5%);
    }
  }

  #grain-overlay .grain-texture {
    position: absolute;
    top: -50%;
    left: -50%;
    width: 200%;
    height: 200%;
    background: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg viewBox='0 0 256 256' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cfilter id='noise'%3E%3CfeTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.65' numOctaves='3' stitchTiles='stitch'/%3E%3C/filter%3E%3Crect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23noise)'/%3E%3C/svg%3E");
    opacity: 0.15;
    animation: hf-grain-noise 0.5s steps(1) infinite;
  }
</style>

The video now has a film grain overlay, but I couldn't render a frame to check it visually: this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg.

I installed the `grain-overlay` component from your project's registry with `npx hyperframes add grain-overlay` and pasted its snippet into `index.html` as the last child of `#main`. It is not a timed clip, so it sits on top of both the title card and the caption for the full 10 seconds.

The component's defaults are unchanged: grain opacity 0.15, a 0.5s jitter loop, and `z-index: 100`. Opacity and speed are both set in the `#grain-overlay .grain-texture` rule if you want it heavier or slower.

`hyperframes lint` reports one error and one warning, both about the composition having no `window.__timelines` registration. Neither comes from the grain overlay, and I left them alone. The linter suggests adding `data-no-timeline` to `#main`, and warns that without it each render waits up to 45 seconds.

The install also added `compositions/components/grain-overlay.html`, a `hyperframes.lock.json`, a `registryItems` entry in `hyperframes.json`, and a `.hyperframes/` cache directory.

<!--
  Grain Overlay — animated film grain texture.

  Usage: paste this snippet into your composition's HTML.
  The overlay covers the full viewport with pointer-events: none
  so it sits on top of all content without blocking interaction.

  Customize:
  - opacity: adjust .grain-texture opacity (default 0.15)
  - speed: change animation duration (default 0.5s)
  - texture: swap the background URL for a different pattern
  - z-index: adjust #grain-overlay z-index to layer correctly
-->

<div
  id="grain-overlay"
  style="
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    pointer-events: none;
    z-index: 100;
  "
>
  <div class="grain-texture"></div>
</div>

<style>
  @keyframes hf-grain-noise {
    0%,
    100% {
      transform: translate(0, 0);
    }
    10% {
      transform: translate(-5%, -5%);
    }
    20% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    30% {
      transform: translate(5%, -10%);
    }
    40% {
      transform: translate(-5%, 15%);
    }
    50% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    60% {
      transform: translate(15%, 0);
    }
    70% {
      transform: translate(0, 10%);
    }
    80% {
      transform: translate(-15%, 0);
    }
    90% {
      transform: translate(10%, 5%);
    }
  }

  #grain-overlay .grain-texture {
    position: absolute;
    top: -50%;
    left: -50%;
    width: 200%;
    height: 200%;
    background: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg viewBox='0 0 256 256' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cfilter id='noise'%3E%3CfeTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.65' numOctaves='3' stitchTiles='stitch'/%3E%3C/filter%3E%3Crect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23noise)'/%3E%3C/svg%3E");
    opacity: 0.15;
    animation: hf-grain-noise 0.5s steps(1) infinite;
  }
</style>

answer:
The film grain overlay is in the composition, but I couldn't render a frame to check it visually: this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg and only 0.2 GB of free disk.

I installed the `grain-overlay` component from your project's registry with `npx hyperframes add grain-overlay` and pasted its snippet into `index.html` as the last child of `#main`. It runs for the whole 10 seconds on top of the title and caption (`z-index: 100`), at the component's defaults: 15% opacity, 0.5s jitter loop.

- **Tuning:** to make the grain stronger or subtler, change `opacity` on `.grain-texture`; the animation duration on the same rule controls the speed.
- **Lint:** `npx hyperframes lint` reports one error and one warning, both about the composition having no `window.__timelines` registration. The file had no timeline script before my change, so I left this alone. The linter's suggested fix is adding `data-no-timeline` to the `#main` element, which also avoids a 45-second wait on every render — say if you want me to add it.
- **New files:** the install also added `compositions/components/grain-overlay.html` (the source snippet), `hyperframes.lock.json` and a `.hyperframes/` cache directory.

<!--
  Grain Overlay — animated film grain texture.

  Usage: paste this snippet into your composition's HTML.
  The overlay covers the full viewport with pointer-events: none
  so it sits on top of all content without blocking interaction.

  Customize:
  - opacity: adjust .grain-texture opacity (default 0.15)
  - speed: change animation duration (default 0.5s)
  - texture: swap the background URL for a different pattern
  - z-index: adjust #grain-overlay z-index to layer correctly
-->

<div
  id="grain-overlay"
  style="
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    pointer-events: none;
    z-index: 100;
  "
>
  <div class="grain-texture"></div>
</div>

<style>
  @keyframes hf-grain-noise {
    0%,
    100% {
      transform: translate(0, 0);
    }
    10% {
      transform: translate(-5%, -5%);
    }
    20% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    30% {
      transform: translate(5%, -10%);
    }
    40% {
      transform: translate(-5%, 15%);
    }
    50% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    60% {
      transform: translate(15%, 0);
    }
    70% {
      transform: translate(0, 10%);
    }
    80% {
      transform: translate(-15%, 0);
    }
    90% {
      transform: translate(10%, 5%);
    }
  }

  #grain-overlay .grain-texture {
    position: absolute;
    top: -50%;
    left: -50%;
    width: 200%;
    height: 200%;
    background: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg viewBox='0 0 256 256' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cfilter id='noise'%3E%3CfeTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.65' numOctaves='3' stitchTiles='stitch'/%3E%3C/filter%3E%3Crect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23noise)'/%3E%3C/svg%3E");
    opacity: 0.15;
    animation: hf-grain-noise 0.5s steps(1) infinite;
  }
</style>

answer:
The video now has an animated film grain overlay across the full frame for its whole duration. I couldn't render it to check visually, because this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg.

What I changed:

- **Installed the component**: I ran `npx hyperframes add grain-overlay`, which pulled the component from your configured registry into `compositions/components/grain-overlay.html`. It also recorded it in `hyperframes.json`, wrote `hyperframes.lock.json` and created a `.hyperframes/` state folder.
- **Pasted it into `index.html`**: the overlay is the last child of `#main`, above the title and caption (`z-index: 100`), with no timing attributes so it stays on throughout.
- **Sized the root**: I added `position:relative; width:1920px; height:1080px; overflow:hidden` to `#main`, so the overlay anchors to the frame and the oversized grain texture is clipped at the edges.

`hyperframes lint` reports one error and one warning, both of which were there before my change: the composition has no `window.__timelines` registration and no `data-no-timeline` attribute. I left that alone. The warning says it adds 45 seconds to every render, and I haven't confirmed that the CSS-driven grain animates in a render without a timeline.

The grain is at the component defaults: opacity `0.15` and a `0.5s` animation cycle, both set on `.grain-texture` in `index.html` if you want it heavier or subtler.

<!--
  Grain Overlay — animated film grain texture.

  Usage: paste this snippet into your composition's HTML.
  The overlay covers the full viewport with pointer-events: none
  so it sits on top of all content without blocking interaction.

  Customize:
  - opacity: adjust .grain-texture opacity (default 0.15)
  - speed: change animation duration (default 0.5s)
  - texture: swap the background URL for a different pattern
  - z-index: adjust #grain-overlay z-index to layer correctly
-->

<div
  id="grain-overlay"
  style="
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    pointer-events: none;
    z-index: 100;
  "
>
  <div class="grain-texture"></div>
</div>

<style>
  @keyframes hf-grain-noise {
    0%,
    100% {
      transform: translate(0, 0);
    }
    10% {
      transform: translate(-5%, -5%);
    }
    20% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    30% {
      transform: translate(5%, -10%);
    }
    40% {
      transform: translate(-5%, 15%);
    }
    50% {
      transform: translate(-10%, 5%);
    }
    60% {
      transform: translate(15%, 0);
    }
    70% {
      transform: translate(0, 10%);
    }
    80% {
      transform: translate(-15%, 0);
    }
    90% {
      transform: translate(10%, 5%);
    }
  }

  #grain-overlay .grain-texture {
    position: absolute;
    top: -50%;
    left: -50%;
    width: 200%;
    height: 200%;
    background: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg viewBox='0 0 256 256' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cfilter id='noise'%3E%3CfeTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.65' numOctaves='3' stitchTiles='stitch'/%3E%3C/filter%3E%3Crect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23noise)'/%3E%3C/svg%3E");
    opacity: 0.15;
    animation: hf-grain-noise 0.5s steps(1) infinite;
  }
</style>

The data chart block is installed and mounted in `index.html` from 2s to 8s, but I couldn't preview or render it — this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg. The only checks I ran were `hyperframes lint` and `hyperframes timeline`: the timeline shows the clip at 2–8s, and lint reports the same error and warning as before my change (the `main` composition has no timeline registration).

What I did:
- **Install:** ran `npx hyperframes add data-chart`, which pulled the block from your configured registry into `compositions/data-chart.html`. It also created `hyperframes.lock.json` and a `.hyperframes/` cache folder in the project.
- **Mount:** added the host element as the last child of `#main` with `data-start="2"`, `data-duration="6"`, on its own track (3).
- **Positioning:** added one CSS rule pinning the chart to the top-left of the frame, so the title and caption above it don't push it down and off the bottom.

Two things you should know before rendering:

1. **The chart's animation is longer than 6 seconds.** The block is authored for 15s and its animation takes about 9.5s to finish. At 6s the bars are complete, but the conversion-rate line is only about half drawn and the source line never appears.
2. **The chart covers the other clips while it's on screen.** It is a full-frame block with an opaque cream background, so it hides the last second of the "Launch" title (2–3s) and the whole "Welcome" caption (3–7s). Layering the text on top wouldn't help as is, since it's near-white on cream.

Decision for you: I left the block's own animation untouched to respect the 6-second length you asked for. If you'd rather see the full chart, I can either compress its animation to fit in 6s or extend the clip to about 9.5s (the video is 10s, so it fits from a 0s start or with a slightly shorter tail). Say which.

          const gridGroup = svg.querySelector(".gridlines");
          const xAxisGroup = svg.querySelector(".x-axis-labels");
          const barsGroup = svg.querySelector(".bars-group");
          const barLabelsGroup = svg.querySelector(".bar-labels-group");
          const lineLabelsGroup = svg.querySelector(".line-labels-group");
          const conversionPath = svg.querySelector(".conversion-path");
          const lineDot = svg.querySelector(".line-dot");

          // Create Gridlines
          for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
            const y = startY - i * (chartHeight / 5);
            const line = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "line");
            line.setAttribute("x1", startX);
            line.setAttribute("y1", y);
            line.setAttribute("x2", startX + chartWidth);
            line.setAttribute("y2", y);
            line.setAttribute("class", "grid-line");
            gridGroup.appendChild(line);
          }

          // Create X-Axis Labels & Bars & Bar Labels
          const linePoints = [];
          months.forEach((month, i) => {
            const x = getX(i);

            const label = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            label.setAttribute("x", x);
            label.setAttribute("y", startY + 30);
            label.setAttribute("class", "axis-label");
            label.textContent = month;
            xAxisGroup.appendChild(label);

            const barHeight = (revenueData[i] / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
            const bar = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
            bar.setAttribute("x", x - barWidth / 2);
            bar.setAttribute("y", startY);
            bar.setAttribute("width", barWidth);
            bar.setAttribute("height", 0);
            bar.setAttribute("class", "bar");
            barsGroup.appendChild(bar);

            const barLabel = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            barLabel.setAttribute("x", x);
            barLabel.setAttribute("y", getBarY(revenueData[i]) - 10);
            barLabel.setAttribute("class", "bar-label");
            barLabel.textContent = `$${revenueData[i]}K`;
            barLabelsGroup.appendChild(barLabel);

            linePoints.push(`${x},${getLineY(conversionData[i])}`);

            const lineLabel = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            lineLabel.setAttribute("x", x);
            lineLabel.setAttribute("y", getLineY(conversionData[i]) - 15);
            lineLabel.setAttribute("class", "line-label");
            lineLabel.textContent = `${conversionData[i]}%`;
            lineLabelsGroup.appendChild(lineLabel);
          });

          // Set Path Data
          conversionPath.setAttribute("d", `M ${linePoints.join(" L ")}`);
          const pathLength = conversionPath.getTotalLength();
          conversionPath.style.strokeDasharray = pathLength;
          conversionPath.style.strokeDashoffset = pathLength;

          // --- ANIMATION TIMELINE ---

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .headline',
            {
              clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)",
              duration: 1.2,
              ease: "power1.inOut",
            },
            0,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .subtitle',
            {
              clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)",
              duration: 1.2,
              ease: "power1.inOut",
            },
            0.2,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.4,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            1.0,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .grid-line',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.5,
              stagger: 0.25,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            0.5,
          );

          // Bars
          const bars = barsGroup.querySelectorAll(".bar");
          const barLabels = barLabelsGroup.querySelectorAll(".bar-label");

          bars.forEach((bar, i) => {
            const barHeight = (revenueData[i] / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
            const startTime = 1.5 + i * 0.5;

            tl.to(
              bar,
              {
                attr: { height: barHeight, y: startY - barHeight },
                duration: 0.8,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              startTime,
            );

            tl.to(
              barLabels[i],
              {
                opacity: 1,
                duration: 0.3,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              startTime + 0.8,
            );
          });

          // Line
          const lastBarStartTime = 1.5 + (months.length - 1) * 0.5;
          const lineStartTime = lastBarStartTime + 0.5;

          tl.to(
            conversionPath,
            {
              strokeDashoffset: 0,
              duration: 3,
              ease: "none",
            },
            lineStartTime,
          );

          // Line Dot & Labels
          tl.set(
            lineDot,
            {
              opacity: 1,
              attr: { cx: getX(0), cy: getLineY(conversionData[0]) },
            },
            lineStartTime,
          );

          const lineLabels = lineLabelsGroup.querySelectorAll(".line-label");
          months.forEach((_, i) => {
            if (i > 0) {
              const x = getX(i);
              const y = getLineY(conversionData[i]);
              tl.to(
                lineDot,
                {
                  attr: { cx: x, cy: y },
                  duration: 3 / (months.length - 1),
                  ease: "none",
                },
                lineStartTime + ((i - 1) / (months.length - 1)) * 3,
              );
            }

            const labelTime = lineStartTime + (i / (months.length - 1)) * 3 + 0.2;

            lineLabels[i].textContent = "0.0%";

            tl.to(
              lineLabels[i],
              {
                opacity: 1,
                duration: 0.1,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              labelTime,
            );

            const dummy = { val: 0 };
            tl.to(
              dummy,
              {
                val: conversionData[i],
                duration: 0.8,
                ease: "power2.out",
                onUpdate: () => {
                  lineLabels[i].textContent = dummy.val.toFixed(1) + "%";
                },
              },
              labelTime,
            );
          });

          // Source Line
          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .source',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.5,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            ">+0.5",
          );

          window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
          window.__timelines["data-chart"] = tl;
        })();
      </script>
    </div>

answer:
The data chart block is installed and placed on the timeline from 2s to 8s (start 2, duration 6), on its own track 3. I couldn't render or snapshot it, because this machine has no Chrome or FFmpeg, so the result is checked only by `hyperframes timeline` and lint.

- **Install:** `hyperframes add data-chart` pulled the block from your project registry into `compositions/data-chart.html`, and added a `registryItems` entry to `hyperframes.json` plus a new `hyperframes.lock.json`.
- **Placement:** one new line in `index.html` after the caption, written like the existing clips (`id`, `class="clip"`, timing attributes).

Things you should know:

- **The chart's animation gets cut off.** The block is built to run 15 seconds, and its animation takes about 9. In a 6-second window the bars finish, but the conversion-rate line is only about half drawn and the source line never appears. Fixing that means either a longer window or retiming the block's animation; I left the block file untouched.
- **It probably covers the other clips.** The chart is full-frame with an opaque background, and it overlaps the title (2–3s) and the whole "Welcome" caption (3–7s). The page has no positioning CSS, so I couldn't confirm how they stack.
- **Lint reports one error that was already there.** `index.html` has no `window.__timelines` registration for the `main` composition; lint flags nothing about the new clip. I didn't change this.

          const gridGroup = svg.querySelector(".gridlines");
          const xAxisGroup = svg.querySelector(".x-axis-labels");
          const barsGroup = svg.querySelector(".bars-group");
          const barLabelsGroup = svg.querySelector(".bar-labels-group");
          const lineLabelsGroup = svg.querySelector(".line-labels-group");
          const conversionPath = svg.querySelector(".conversion-path");
          const lineDot = svg.querySelector(".line-dot");

          // Create Gridlines
          for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
            const y = startY - i * (chartHeight / 5);
            const line = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "line");
            line.setAttribute("x1", startX);
            line.setAttribute("y1", y);
            line.setAttribute("x2", startX + chartWidth);
            line.setAttribute("y2", y);
            line.setAttribute("class", "grid-line");
            gridGroup.appendChild(line);
          }

          // Create X-Axis Labels & Bars & Bar Labels
          const linePoints = [];
          months.forEach((month, i) => {
            const x = getX(i);

            const label = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            label.setAttribute("x", x);
            label.setAttribute("y", startY + 30);
            label.setAttribute("class", "axis-label");
            label.textContent = month;
            xAxisGroup.appendChild(label);

            const barHeight = (revenueData[i] / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
            const bar = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
            bar.setAttribute("x", x - barWidth / 2);
            bar.setAttribute("y", startY);
            bar.setAttribute("width", barWidth);
            bar.setAttribute("height", 0);
            bar.setAttribute("class", "bar");
            barsGroup.appendChild(bar);

            const barLabel = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            barLabel.setAttribute("x", x);
            barLabel.setAttribute("y", getBarY(revenueData[i]) - 10);
            barLabel.setAttribute("class", "bar-label");
            barLabel.textContent = `$${revenueData[i]}K`;
            barLabelsGroup.appendChild(barLabel);

            linePoints.push(`${x},${getLineY(conversionData[i])}`);

            const lineLabel = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            lineLabel.setAttribute("x", x);
            lineLabel.setAttribute("y", getLineY(conversionData[i]) - 15);
            lineLabel.setAttribute("class", "line-label");
            lineLabel.textContent = `${conversionData[i]}%`;
            lineLabelsGroup.appendChild(lineLabel);
          });

          // Set Path Data
          conversionPath.setAttribute("d", `M ${linePoints.join(" L ")}`);
          const pathLength = conversionPath.getTotalLength();
          conversionPath.style.strokeDasharray = pathLength;
          conversionPath.style.strokeDashoffset = pathLength;

          // --- ANIMATION TIMELINE ---

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .headline',
            {
              clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)",
              duration: 1.2,
              ease: "power1.inOut",
            },
            0,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .subtitle',
            {
              clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)",
              duration: 1.2,
              ease: "power1.inOut",
            },
            0.2,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.4,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            1.0,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .grid-line',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.5,
              stagger: 0.25,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            0.5,
          );

          // Bars
          const bars = barsGroup.querySelectorAll(".bar");
          const barLabels = barLabelsGroup.querySelectorAll(".bar-label");

          bars.forEach((bar, i) => {
            const barHeight = (revenueData[i] / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
            const startTime = 1.5 + i * 0.5;

            tl.to(
              bar,
              {
                attr: { height: barHeight, y: startY - barHeight },
                duration: 0.8,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              startTime,
            );

            tl.to(
              barLabels[i],
              {
                opacity: 1,
                duration: 0.3,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              startTime + 0.8,
            );
          });

          // Line
          const lastBarStartTime = 1.5 + (months.length - 1) * 0.5;
          const lineStartTime = lastBarStartTime + 0.5;

          tl.to(
            conversionPath,
            {
              strokeDashoffset: 0,
              duration: 3,
              ease: "none",
            },
            lineStartTime,
          );

          // Line Dot & Labels
          tl.set(
            lineDot,
            {
              opacity: 1,
              attr: { cx: getX(0), cy: getLineY(conversionData[0]) },
            },
            lineStartTime,
          );

          const lineLabels = lineLabelsGroup.querySelectorAll(".line-label");
          months.forEach((_, i) => {
            if (i > 0) {
              const x = getX(i);
              const y = getLineY(conversionData[i]);
              tl.to(
                lineDot,
                {
                  attr: { cx: x, cy: y },
                  duration: 3 / (months.length - 1),
                  ease: "none",
                },
                lineStartTime + ((i - 1) / (months.length - 1)) * 3,
              );
            }

            const labelTime = lineStartTime + (i / (months.length - 1)) * 3 + 0.2;

            lineLabels[i].textContent = "0.0%";

            tl.to(
              lineLabels[i],
              {
                opacity: 1,
                duration: 0.1,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              labelTime,
            );

            const dummy = { val: 0 };
            tl.to(
              dummy,
              {
                val: conversionData[i],
                duration: 0.8,
                ease: "power2.out",
                onUpdate: () => {
                  lineLabels[i].textContent = dummy.val.toFixed(1) + "%";
                },
              },
              labelTime,
            );
          });

          // Source Line
          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .source',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.5,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            ">+0.5",
          );

          window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
          window.__timelines["data-chart"] = tl;
        })();
      </script>
    </div>

      rel="stylesheet"
    />
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      * {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }
      html,
      body {

  <body>
    <div
      id="data-chart"
      data-composition-id="data-chart"
      data-width="1920"
      data-height="1080"
      data-start="0"
      data-duration="15"
    >
      <div class="chart-container">
        <!-- Header Section -->
        <div class="header">
          <h1 class="headline">Monthly Revenue vs. Conversion Rate</h1>
          <p class="subtitle">Jan–Jun 2024, in thousands</p>
          <div class="key">
            <div class="key-item">
              <div class="key-box revenue-box"></div>
              <span class="key-text">Revenue</span>
            </div>
            <div class="key-item">
              <div class="key-line conversion-line"></div>
              <span class="key-text">Conversion Rate</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <!-- SVG Chart Area -->
        <svg class="chart-svg" viewBox="0 0 1600 700" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
          <!-- Gridlines Group -->
          <g class="gridlines"></g>

          <!-- X-Axis Labels -->
          <g class="x-axis-labels"></g>

          <!-- Bars Group (Revenue) -->
          <g class="bars-group"></g>

          <!-- Bar Labels Group -->
          <g class="bar-labels-group"></g>

          <!-- Line Group (Conversion Rate) -->
          <g class="line-group">
            <path class="conversion-path" fill="none" stroke="#326FA8" stroke-width="1.5" />
            <circle class="line-dot" r="5" fill="#326FA8" style="opacity: 0" />
          </g>

          <!-- Line Labels Group -->
          <g class="line-labels-group"></g>

          <!-- Baseline -->
          <line x1="100" y1="600" x2="1500" y2="600" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" />
        </svg>

        <!-- Source Line -->
        <div class="source">Source: Internal analytics</div>
      </div>

      <style>
        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] {
          width: 1920px;
          height: 1080px;
          background-color: #faf9f6;
          font-family: "Libre Franklin", sans-serif;
          color: #333;
          display: flex;
          justify-content: center;
          align-items: center;
          overflow: hidden;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .chart-container {
          width: 1600px;
          height: 900px;
          display: flex;
          flex-direction: column;
          position: relative;
          transform: scale(1.15);
          transform-origin: center center;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .header {
          margin-bottom: 40px;
          text-align: left;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .headline {
          font-family: "Libre Baskerville", serif;
          font-size: 42px;
          margin: 0;
          padding: 0;
          clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0);
          white-space: nowrap;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .subtitle {
          font-size: 16px;
          color: #666;
          margin: 8px 0 16px 0;
          clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0);
          white-space: nowrap;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key {
          display: flex;
          gap: 24px;
          opacity: 0;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key-item {
          display: flex;
          align-items: center;
          gap: 8px;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key-box {
          width: 10px;
          height: 10px;
          background-color: #5c5c5c;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key-line {
          width: 16px;
          height: 1.5px;
          background-color: #326fa8;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key-text {
          font-size: 13px;
          color: #666;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .chart-svg {
          width: 100%;
          height: 600px;
          overflow: visible;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .source {
          position: absolute;
          bottom: 0;
          left: 0;
          font-size: 11px;
          color: #999;
          opacity: 0;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .grid-line {
          stroke: #e8e8e8;
          stroke-width: 0.5px;
          opacity: 0;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .axis-label {
          font-size: 14px;
          fill: #666;
          text-anchor: middle;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .bar {
          fill: #5c5c5c;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .bar-label {
          font-size: 14px;
          fill: #333;
          text-anchor: middle;
          opacity: 0;
        }

        [data-composition-id="data-chart"] .line-label {
          font-size: 14px;
          fill: #326fa8;
          font-weight: 600;
          text-anchor: middle;
          opacity: 0;
        }
      </style>

      <script>
        (function () {
          const svg = document.querySelector('[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .chart-svg');
          const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

          // Data
          const months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"];
          const revenueData = [8, 12, 15, 11, 18, 22];
          const conversionData = [2.1, 2.8, 3.2, 2.9, 3.8, 4.2];

          // Chart Dimensions
          const chartWidth = 1400;
          const chartHeight = 500;
          const startX = 100;
          const startY = 600;
          const barWidth = 80;
          const spacing = (chartWidth - barWidth * months.length) / (months.length + 1);

          // Scales
          const maxRevenue = 25;
          const maxConversion = 5;

          const getBarY = (val) => startY - (val / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
          const getLineY = (val) => startY - (val / maxConversion) * chartHeight;
          const getX = (i) => startX + spacing + i * (barWidth + spacing) + barWidth / 2;

          // Setup Elements
          const gridGroup = svg.querySelector(".gridlines");
          const xAxisGroup = svg.querySelector(".x-axis-labels");
          const barsGroup = svg.querySelector(".bars-group");
          const barLabelsGroup = svg.querySelector(".bar-labels-group");
          const lineLabelsGroup = svg.querySelector(".line-labels-group");
          const conversionPath = svg.querySelector(".conversion-path");
          const lineDot = svg.querySelector(".line-dot");

          // Create Gridlines
          for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
            const y = startY - i * (chartHeight / 5);
            const line = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "line");
            line.setAttribute("x1", startX);
            line.setAttribute("y1", y);
            line.setAttribute("x2", startX + chartWidth);
            line.setAttribute("y2", y);
            line.setAttribute("class", "grid-line");
            gridGroup.appendChild(line);
          }

          // Create X-Axis Labels & Bars & Bar Labels
          const linePoints = [];
          months.forEach((month, i) => {
            const x = getX(i);

            const label = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            label.setAttribute("x", x);
            label.setAttribute("y", startY + 30);
            label.setAttribute("class", "axis-label");
            label.textContent = month;
            xAxisGroup.appendChild(label);

            const barHeight = (revenueData[i] / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
            const bar = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
            bar.setAttribute("x", x - barWidth / 2);
            bar.setAttribute("y", startY);
            bar.setAttribute("width", barWidth);
            bar.setAttribute("height", 0);
            bar.setAttribute("class", "bar");
            barsGroup.appendChild(bar);

            const barLabel = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            barLabel.setAttribute("x", x);
            barLabel.setAttribute("y", getBarY(revenueData[i]) - 10);
            barLabel.setAttribute("class", "bar-label");
            barLabel.textContent = `$${revenueData[i]}K`;
            barLabelsGroup.appendChild(barLabel);

            linePoints.push(`${x},${getLineY(conversionData[i])}`);

            const lineLabel = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
            lineLabel.setAttribute("x", x);
            lineLabel.setAttribute("y", getLineY(conversionData[i]) - 15);
            lineLabel.setAttribute("class", "line-label");
            lineLabel.textContent = `${conversionData[i]}%`;
            lineLabelsGroup.appendChild(lineLabel);
          });

          // Set Path Data
          conversionPath.setAttribute("d", `M ${linePoints.join(" L ")}`);
          const pathLength = conversionPath.getTotalLength();
          conversionPath.style.strokeDasharray = pathLength;
          conversionPath.style.strokeDashoffset = pathLength;

          // --- ANIMATION TIMELINE ---

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .headline',
            {
              clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)",
              duration: 1.2,
              ease: "power1.inOut",
            },
            0,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .subtitle',
            {
              clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)",
              duration: 1.2,
              ease: "power1.inOut",
            },
            0.2,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .key',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.4,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            1.0,
          );

          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .grid-line',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.5,
              stagger: 0.25,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            0.5,
          );

          // Bars
          const bars = barsGroup.querySelectorAll(".bar");
          const barLabels = barLabelsGroup.querySelectorAll(".bar-label");

          bars.forEach((bar, i) => {
            const barHeight = (revenueData[i] / maxRevenue) * chartHeight;
            const startTime = 1.5 + i * 0.5;

            tl.to(
              bar,
              {
                attr: { height: barHeight, y: startY - barHeight },
                duration: 0.8,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              startTime,
            );

            tl.to(
              barLabels[i],
              {
                opacity: 1,
                duration: 0.3,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              startTime + 0.8,
            );
          });

          // Line
          const lastBarStartTime = 1.5 + (months.length - 1) * 0.5;
          const lineStartTime = lastBarStartTime + 0.5;

          tl.to(
            conversionPath,
            {
              strokeDashoffset: 0,
              duration: 3,
              ease: "none",
            },
            lineStartTime,
          );

          // Line Dot & Labels
          tl.set(
            lineDot,
            {
              opacity: 1,
              attr: { cx: getX(0), cy: getLineY(conversionData[0]) },
            },
            lineStartTime,
          );

          const lineLabels = lineLabelsGroup.querySelectorAll(".line-label");
          months.forEach((_, i) => {
            if (i > 0) {
              const x = getX(i);
              const y = getLineY(conversionData[i]);
              tl.to(
                lineDot,
                {
                  attr: { cx: x, cy: y },
                  duration: 3 / (months.length - 1),
                  ease: "none",
                },
                lineStartTime + ((i - 1) / (months.length - 1)) * 3,
              );
            }

            const labelTime = lineStartTime + (i / (months.length - 1)) * 3 + 0.2;

            lineLabels[i].textContent = "0.0%";

            tl.to(
              lineLabels[i],
              {
                opacity: 1,
                duration: 0.1,
                ease: "power2.out",
              },
              labelTime,
            );

            const dummy = { val: 0 };
            tl.to(
              dummy,
              {
                val: conversionData[i],
                duration: 0.8,
                ease: "power2.out",
                onUpdate: () => {
                  lineLabels[i].textContent = dummy.val.toFixed(1) + "%";
                },
              },
              labelTime,
            );
          });

          // Source Line
          tl.to(
            '[data-composition-id="data-chart"] .source',
            {
              opacity: 1,
              duration: 0.5,
              ease: "power2.out",
            },
            ">+0.5",
          );

          window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
          window.__timelines["data-chart"] = tl;
        })();
      </script>
    </div>
